shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials are rising as buying interest grows for grades located away from disruptions in the Middle East.

children: West African crude oil differentials are rising as buying interest grows for grades located away from disruptions in the Middle East.
Nigerian crude sellers were quoting Qua Iboe at dated Brent plus $6 and Bonga at dated plus $9, a trader in the West African market told Reuters on Tuesday.
That is unchanged from where Bonga was heard offered last week. Forcados was heard on offer at around dated plus $8 last week according to traders.
West African differentials are drawing strength from disruptions to supplies in the Middle East.
The large volume of cargoes the Dangote refinery is taking is also leaving less supply available to other buyers.

Fuel shortages are expected to persist long after the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran due to the damage inflicted on refineries and the need to replenish stocks, David Bird, the chief executive officer of Nigeria's Dangote oil refinery, told Reuters ahead of the company's IPO next week.
The Dangote oil refinery is currently running at full capacity, 700,000 bpd, he added.
